question_text: Write the SI unit and dimensional formula of torque. Is torque the same physical quantity as work?

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Unit and dimensions

lines.text: SI unit: N·m;  dimensions: [M L² T⁻²]

steps.why: The dimensional formula follows from τ = rF — the same product of a force and a length that work is built from.
common_mistakes: Writing the unit as joule. Torque is deliberately kept as N·m.

recall.must_convey: That torque is in newton metre with dimensions M L squared T minus 2.
accept: M L squared T minus two

steps.label: Torque vs work
lines: No. Work is a SCALAR (a dot product);
torque is a VECTOR (a cross product).
steps.why: A favourite trap: identical dimensions never make two quantities the same — the vector character separates them.
common_mistakes: Concluding they are the same because the dimensions match.

recall.must_convey: That work is a scalar and torque a vector — same dimensions, different quantities.
accept: work is a scalar torque is a vector
